launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋\
We're [Naveen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/naveen-qureshi) & [Frederik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frederik-vanhevel/), fintech founders and operators building [Rapidfolio](https://rapidfolio.com/).\
\
**TL;DR:** Rapidfolio automates the most complex manual compliance, operations, and fraud processes that analysts perform at fintechs and banks today. We do this with 100% accuracy, speed, and auditability. We are previous founders and operators in fintech, and created Rapidfolio because we wished it existed when we were running Sable (S19).\
\
**Video:**\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0UBIfRhNh08>

\
**Our Ask:**\
**If you are a founder or operator at a fintech** **or bank** **who**\
i) has a pressing need to automate manual tasks due to high volume and/or,\
ii) needs to decrease the amount you spend annually on back-office staff or\
iii) you simply want to build solid automation to decrease human error\
Reach out directly: [founders@rapidfolio.com](mailto:founders@rapidfolio.com) or book a demo: <https://cal.com/naveen-qureshi/demo>

**——————-**

**The Problem** 

Fintechs and banks spend up to **30% of their revenue** on operations, compliance, risk and fraud back-office staff. The back-office performs manual processes like KYC and KYB reviews, OFAC/sanctions/watchlist reviews, fraud investigations, disputes and chargebacks, mortgage and loan underwriting, and sometimes even manual data input workflows, among others. The back-office scales as a function of the number of accounts held at the fintech/bank and quickly becomes extremely costly, time consuming, and error prone. 

Frederik and I lived this problem firsthand. **We started Rapidfolio because we wished it existed when we were running Sable (S19)!**

**Our Solution** 

Rapidfolio turns manual compliance, operations, risk and fraud processes into accurate, auditable, and automated flows. We’re running at **100% accuracy** in production. We provide the **end to end platform and services** to:

**1. Convert your existing procedure** into deterministic, automated, workflows in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106986&key=user_uploads/334623/8df4940f-c6ec-41e1-a6a5-4ccd6476667b)

**2.** We generate dozens of **test cases**, including edge cases, and fully test the workflow.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106986&key=user_uploads/334623/940aa8f9-9728-47ef-9a5c-81648c0b28b8)

**3.** Once tested, you can **trigger the workflow** to run it in whichever way you prefer - be it API, our scheduler, a JIRA ticket.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106986&key=user_uploads/334623/2ee48bae-3d66-487c-9e70-9ab859eb0b02)

**4. You have full visibility and control:** all workflows are version controlled, and each action is auditable and traceable. You can include humans-in-the-loop where needed. All analytics live directly in your dashboard.

Rapidfolio provides “innate abilities” like automated web browsing, document reading/analysis, comprehensive summaries, human-level judgment, to name a few. Additionally, Rapidfolio integrates easily into your **existing tech stack**. We have built-in integrations with leadings operations, compliance and fraud vendors in the financial services industry.

We are SOC 2 compliant, and are **live with customers across the U.S. and Canada.**

\
**The Team:**

**Naveen Qureshi:** CEO and co-founder, Rapidfolio\
Previously was co-founder & CEO of Sable (S19) that I built, scaled and sold. After Sable’s exit, I built and launched additional credit products with [Seen.com](http://Seen.com). Ex Capital One, Amazon, Target. Columbia Business School.\
\
**Frederik Vanhevel:** CTO and co-founder, Rapidfolio\
Previously built the entire banking stack for two fintechs from scratch. First, as founding engineer at Sable (S19), where he shipped the entire banking stack in a record 3 months, pre-AI. And after Sable’s exit, with Seen.com. Fred also built internal tools for back-office staff at both fintechs, and is passionate about automating the more tedious workflows with Rapidfolio.\
\
Reach out directly: [founders@rapidfolio.com](mailto:founders@rapidfolio.com) or book a demo: <https://cal.com/naveen-qureshi/demo>

launches.title: Grade: Performance based Payroll
launches.tagline: Helping companies pay their workers based on performance.
launches.body:
**Lotanna** and **James** here, co-founders at Grade (YC W26).

Grade is performance based payroll. We help companies pay workers based on results.

### 

### **Our Launch Video 🎥**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wbNeaDNaQKY>

### **The Problem ❌**

Payroll is huge. About $50T a year goes to worker pay worldwide. But most payroll systems still pay people for hours worked, even when hours do not match real output.

When companies try to pay on performance, it gets messy fast:

* The rules live in spreadsheets
* Approvals are manual
* Payouts are slow and mistakes happen

### **Our Unique Insight 💡**

Before Grade, we built, scaled, and exited 4 mobile AI apps. Creators were our main growth channel, and they helped us reach millions of users.

Paying creators was always a gamble. We paid a flat fee up front and hoped a video went viral. When we switched to paying for views instead, scaling got easy, but the tools were still spreadsheets. There was no payroll system for performance pay.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97852&key=user_uploads/1159814/0f8e12e4-c2c3-4a41-ad24-ff24b323d164)

### **The Solution ✅**

Grade makes performance pay run like real payroll, starting with creators.

* Pay creators any way you want (flat fees, performance pay, bonused)
* We track performance and calculate payouts automatically
* Approve and pay out in bulk, we deal with all the invoices and tax complaince

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97852&key=user_uploads/1159814/58ba3703-1ad5-40d8-9416-24b28145fa41)

### **Traction 📊**

In the last 30 days, companies used Grade to **pay out $380k+** to creators, up 120% MoM

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97852&key=user_uploads/1159814/07111969-8895-4c5e-99f2-d8e6606424d5)

### **Our ask 📣**

If your company is paying creators at scale and you want pay tied to results without the spreadsheet mess, we would love to talk.

[usegrade.com](http://usegrade.com)

launches.title: Hedge: AI-native specialty insurance company
launches.tagline: Helping brokers get faster and better coverage for their customers
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We help insurance brokerages get quotes faster and cheaper. We started as brokers, realized insurance is broken end to end, and are now building the plumbing to fix it.

We’re hiring across sales, ops, and engineering here in SF. [**Apply here**](https://www.workatastartup.com/companies/hedge)**.** 

### **The problem:**

I started a YC-backed AI-native insurance brokerage because buying insurance sucked.

We thought the answer was building a better brokerage. But then we became brokers and realized we weren’t actually fixing the system.

Brokers do important work. They help businesses navigate a messy market. But they don’t control the parts of the stack that determine speed, price, and coverage.

Every quote still depends on multiple layers of brokers, underwriters, carriers, reinsurers, MGAs, and wholesalers.

Each layer is still manual. Someone re-enters the same information by hand, then emails it to another person in the chain who does the same.

Even when brokers move fast, quotes still sometimes take days or weeks. Brokers hate this. Their customers hate it even more.

We realized the only way to fix this was to go full stack and rebuild the workflows ourselves.

### **What we’re building:**

[**Hedge**](https://www.hedgespecialty.com) helps insurance brokerages get better, faster, and cheaper coverage for complex businesses.

To do this, we’re starting with the wholesale layer. The first major bottleneck for brokers.

Our competitors are billion-dollar businesses that are still almost entirely human-driven. Ryan Specialty, one of the largest wholesalers, spends almost 60% of revenue on salaries. Their version of innovation is giving manual work to offshore contractors.

We think the better version is rebuilding the workflow around AI from day one. Hedge uses AI agents paired with underwriting to help brokers get quotes faster.

Soon, we’re moving up the stack: combining wholesale distribution and underwriting into one AI-native insurance company built to help brokers win more business.

### **Let’s talk!**

We’re already working with some of the fastest-growing brokerages we know, and now we’re scaling as fast as possible.

If you place E&S business and want faster, cheaper quotes for your clients, we’d love to work with you.\
\
To learn more:[ hedgespecialty.com](https://www.hedgespecialty.com/)\
\
**We’re hiring!  [Apply here](https://www.hedgespecialty.com/careers)**

launches.title: WithAI – Custom command centers for hedge funds
launches.tagline: We help institutional investors research stocks and track their portfolio using AI.
launches.body:
We're Ian and Ben, co-founders of WithAI. WithAI helps institutional investors use AI to research stocks and manage their portfolios. We forward-deploy to set up Multiplier, a secure platform that teaches AI how the fund works and connects it to all the needed tools, files, data, and context, so that investors can use the full strength of today's agents without taking on a second job as Claude-wrangler. After three months, we're live with multiple clients, doing >$100k ARR. If you know a fundamental equity investor, we'd love to meet them. Email [ian@withai.co](mailto:ian@withai.co).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_ZhD9Y60GQ>

AI has radically transformed coding. But in finance, super-sharp, highly-paid people are spending 2026 combing through an inbox full of PDFs, updating models in Excel, and eyeballing Bloomberg charts. Multiplier packages everything necessary to change that! It includes secure inference endpoints, changelogs, ontology maintainance, guardrails, and VM infrastructure, and it's all hosted on client servers. With a mix of open-source protocols and WithAI elbow grease, Multiplier connects to all the research, tools, and data used at a given firm. We conduct face-to-face interviews so we can give AI the tacit knowledge it needs to work at _your fund specifically_; gaps get filled by user feedback to the AI. Our interface––more like an IDE than a collection of chatboxes––makes oversight, guidance, and participation natural. Early clients have called Multiplier "a tremendous proprietary knowledge flywheel" and "hugely insightful, a massive force multiplier." (In fact, that's where we got the name.) 

Ben and Ian became fast friends building a deeptech investment group together (still going strong) and reunited because they'd independently hit on this idea. Ben, working on enterprise AI as founding researcher at Sentient Labs, saw what stopped his clients from accelerating like his engineers and wanted to productize the solution for the industry he knew best––investing. Ian, (profitably) overseeing an (undisclosably large) equity book at Bridgewater Associates, hacked together AI tools to help himself. They had a call to catch up one night and were spooked how they'd come to the same ideas.

If you know someone who picks stocks for a living (at a hedge fund, mutual fund, family office, etc.), we'd love to meet them. Get in touch at [ian@withai.co](mailto:ian@withai.co). Thanks so much!

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103281&key=user_uploads/3226721/30408a2d-dd8a-47e8-a0b7-b6c76f94eee2)

_We hesitated between rap and insurance…_

Previously, we hit $1M in annual revenue building insurance workflows for brokers. Then we realized **the bigger opportunity was replacing them.**

In the US, there are 36 million SMBs, and 77% are underinsured because distribution is broken. Brokers can’t serve low-premium SMBs profitably: a $2K policy takes almost as much work as a $20K one.

Kinro changes that. Our AI agents handle the full broker workflow 24/7, from finding prospects to binding policies.

In 3 weeks, we got licensed in 30 states, appointed by 15 carriers, and **we bound the first-ever autonomously sold insurance policy.**

Before Kinro, [Pierre-Alexandre](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pakamienny/) was an AI researcher at DeepMind (post-training Gemini on financial services). [Parth Ainampudi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/partha42/) led ML infra at Zoox and I was Chief Insurance Officer at an MGA (insurtech).

**Asks**

If you ever need commercial insurance and want us to shop for you, hit us at [kinro.com](http://kinro.com) (yes we bought the domain for $25k, story [here](https://x.com/pierrealexai/status/2060382045571072043))! 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103281&key=user_uploads/2043734/bac0ad88-22f1-4376-accb-852778c22c1e)

_Post-pivot, Kinro goes to Atlanta to work for 48 straight hours with a retail broker specialized in selling to residential contractors._

**Q&A**

_“Why pivot?”_

We entered YC with a signed $1M enterprise sale to the 2nd largest auto-insurance comparator in the US a few days before (and a third of that money was wired). 

First OH, [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) asked us _“Why not become a broker directly?”_. 

We told him we thought we could reproduce that sale with other brokers and maybe carriers. A month in, we hadn’t yet reproduced the same feat (though we had secured a pilot with the 3rd insurance broker on Earth: WTW). It became more and more obvious that integrations were deep (and FDE intensive) and enterprise sales were endless.

What felt most off was the gap between what we were doing and our long-term vision: helping small business owners and individuals find the right insurance, wherever they are and whenever they need it.

_“So why not just build that?”_  \
\
We always knew we would eventually. Selling to brokers gave us a way to learn while getting paid. But we realized we weren’t learning as fast as we would by building directly for the people we ultimately wanted to serve.

1.5 months later, we came back to him _“Nicolas, we want to become brokers… and this $1M is bad for us”_, he simply answered _“Oh I told you guys, this was obvious”_ (LOL). Walking away from >1M+ from all our clients felt easier after talking about this to [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) and [@Mathilde Collin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/43195). Without YC, we would have waited much longer.

_“What types of insurance do you sell?”_

We sell small business insurance (General Liability, Business Owner’s policy, Worker’s compensation, Commercial Auto…). We focus on admitted markets where checking carriers' appetite and getting quotes can be fully automated with no communication with carriers.

**This new launch video as embarrassing as it is is worth watching! Send us a text if you want your angels to take care of your business.**

Shielded helps manufacturers understand and act on supply chain risk in real time.

As the world has become more volatile, businesses need a tool to monitor events and rapidly take action. Founder James Simon saw this problem first hand in commodities trading, in fact his whole job was to take advantage of other firms reacting too slowly as the world changed. 

That’s what inspired him to build Shielded, as an intelligence layer that integrates quickly, deeply understands your specific business, and turns volatility into clear, proactive decisions.

Shielded supports critical part and supplier management for leading defense companies, ingredient price audits for multinational CPG firms, and tariff impact analysis for global manufacturers.

With API, MCP, BOM, and spreadsheet integrations, every customer deployment to date has taken less than 72 hours.

Instead of simply receiving an alert when something happens, Shielded gives procurement, finance, and supply chain teams company-specific guidance on the impacts of external events, market shifts, and regulation changes, and recommends the right operational or hedging responses.

Shielded is your supply chain’s command center that never sleeps.

launches.title: Audun: AI-native debt collection
launches.tagline: Full-stack AI debt collection company
launches.body:
A letter arrives in the mail.

Impossible to understand.

Another one.

Then the phone calls start.

Once a day. Unpleasant, sometimes hostile.

This is how debt collection works in 2026.

**We’re here to fix it.**\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv/view?usp=sharing)

# TL;DR

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. Our agents automate the collections process end to end, from reminders and negotiations to back-office and legal work. This reduces collection costs for creditors, and enables humans to spend their time on the conversations that matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111293&key=user_uploads/3587634/839f47e4-cdd7-45ed-befd-c621930fef65)

# Ask

We’re looking for introductions to collection leaders at banks, lenders, utilities, telcos, and other high-volume creditors.

# The problem

The debt collection industry is broken. It runs on call centers, paper letters, and software built in the 90s. While the rest of the world is preparing for AGI, the topic of the industry is still email and cloud.

All these inefficiencies ultimately end up with the consumer: incomprehensible letters arriving by snail mail, hostile phone calls, and fees stacking up on a bill they may never have seen. They're paying the cost of an archaic system.

# The solution

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. We automate up to 90% of cases across the whole business, from front to back office. Our agents manage reminders, negotiations, payment plans, and settlements across voice, SMS, email, and WhatsApp. They operate within creditor-defined rules, log every action, and escalate sensitive cases to humans with the full context attached. Behind the scenes, they handle tasks such as skip tracing, payment verification, and legal document drafting.

By automating the grunt work of collections, Audun lowers collection costs for creditors and, ultimately, borrowing costs for consumers. We enable people to focus on the conversations that matter, where human judgment is still required, giving customers the treatment they deserve.

We started out in the Nordics, which has some of the strictest collections regulation in the world. Compliance is critical in this industry, so we built our agents to handle the toughest version of it first. 

# Who we are

We’re four founders with experience across McKinsey, Midjourney, and Norway’s first unicorn. We’ve seen firsthand how manual this industry is, and how stuck the incumbents are. We decided to build the company this industry needs from the ground up.

launches.title: Stoa: The market behind AI hardware
launches.tagline: GPU marketplace where vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. $300M+ in RFQs in our first month.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI hardware trades over phone calls and forwarded spreadsheets. No venue, no price to mark against: lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals. We're building Stoa, an RFQ marketplace where buyers and sellers get firm quotes within 48 hours, and settled trades build the prices the market can mark, finance, and hedge against.

<https://youtu.be/zbD21BgAo88>

GPU deals close in group chats. We know because we've been in them.

A price arrives as a voice note. Someone forwards an inventory list, then it gets forwarded again, and soon three brokers are offering the same machines. Nobody knows who actually owns what or whether any quote is firm.

The market behind those chats is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals, not trades.

We're Berat, Eren, and Kaan. We're building Stoa.

AI hardware is becoming an asset class, but its market is missing the basics: a venue where hardware can trade, prices that buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against, and eventually financing and hedging built on those prices. We're starting with the venue: an RFQ marketplace for GPUs. It gets buyers and sellers firm quotes, and every bid and settlement builds the history the rest needs.

**Here's how it works**

Post what you want to buy or sell: B300s, H200s, H100s, a bare card or a full cluster, new or secondary.

Vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. Instead of spending weeks calling around, you get through the RFQ in 48 hours.

We handle the unglamorous parts too: KYB and counterparty checks, contracts, shipping, and settlement.

In our first month, $300M+ in RFQs ran through the book.

**Why the marketplace comes first**

Ask what an H100 is worth and everyone you call gives you a different answer.

On Stoa, dealers quote against the same RFQ without seeing each other's bids. Because every RFQ, firm quote, award, and settlement runs through us, we see what the hardware actually trades for.

A quote is an opinion. A settled trade is a receipt.

That transaction history becomes prices buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against. Once marks are grounded in settled trades, financing and hedging can follow.

Platts started printing oil prices in a magazine. Kelley Blue Book began as one dealer's published list of what he'd pay for cars. GPU inventory is still being passed around in forwarded spreadsheets, and Blackwell upgrades are now pushing H100 fleets into the secondary market.

Someone is going to be the price.

**The team**

We've known each other for more than ten years. We have founded companies, traded interest rate derivatives, and built trading and pricing infrastructure for oil and gas. Now we're building it for AI hardware.

**Buying or selling?**

If you're buying GPUs or compute, or you're sitting on hardware, sign up at [stoaexchange.com](http://stoaexchange.com).

**Schedule a call: [https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro](https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro)**

**Email us: [founders@stoaexchange.com](mailto:founders@stoaexchange.com)**

**Text or call us:** +1 510 605 3844

And if you know infrastructure heads at neoclouds or data centers, hyperscaler capex teams, dealers, ITADs, or credit desks lending against GPUs, please send this their way.

Berat, Eren & Kaan

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

launches.tagline: The most accurate AI agents for financial reporting
launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105798&key=user_uploads/2947446/1b80714c-9a38-4d02-a037-ab05ad2c9205)

launches.tagline: Veltha reduces six hours of adjuster work to 10 minutes, with adjusters still making the final call
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Veltha reads an entire claim file, flags what's missing, and applies the exact federal regulation that governs it, producing a citation-backed determination a human adjuster just signs off on. Work that took an adjuster \~6 hours now takes \~10 minutes.** Starting with workers' comp and crop insurance.

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

1 in 4 claims adjusters expect to retire within five years. Experienced adjusters are retiring faster than carriers can replace them, and processing capacity is now the binding constraint on growth.

**What we built**

Veltha is an AI claims adjuster that runs the whole file end to end:

* **Triage** - reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection** - checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review** - applies the relevant federal rulebook, and produces a determination where **every output element is tied to a source span and a specific regulatory provision.**

The adjuster's job shifts from _doing_ the claim to _reviewing_ Veltha's output. Less chasing. Faster decisions. Output that survives an audit.

**What we understand that others don't: regulation is the moat, not the obstacle.** Horizontal platforms (Guidewire, Duck Creek) and generic AI-claims startups can summarize a claim file. They can't tell you _which_ provision triggered _which_ adjustment, with citations. We treat the federal rulebook as an anchor for the workflow we embed within the organisation. That's the difference between a summary a human re-does from scratch and an output an adjuster will actually sign.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* **Anyone in claims at a carrier, MGA, or TPA** - especially **workers' comp**
* **People at large self-insured employers** with claims-heavy, high-risk workforces - Companies exactly like these are who we're built for: **Disney, Marriott, Ford, PG&E, Caterpillar**. If you know someone at that kind of company, an intro is gold.

Reach us at [edin@veltha.ai](mailto:edin@veltha.ai) or ping us here. Thanks YC 🙏

**The problem:** Proxy voting at publicly traded companies drives trillions in market value every year. Shareholder votes decide $100B mergers, trillion-dollar pay packages, and the boardroom battles that define companies.

Yet the work is brutally manual: reviewing thousands of pages of SEC filings, research, and engagement notes that live in a patchwork of PDFs, spreadsheets, and post-it notes. And for professional advice, the market has relied on two firms, ISS and Glass Lewis, for 40+ years, a duopoly that controls 97% of the market.

**Why Now:** Technological change and market sentiment are ripping this market wide open.

CEOs have been sounding the proxy-advisor alarm for years:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/45604eff-9d48-4271-90ed-b3bf6000b461)

\
**Why Pennant is better:** Pennant isn't a better proxy advisor. We're building something bigger: the AI-native operating system for corporate governance, built by former proxy voters and technologists, a team that cast these votes and shipped the software at institutional scale.

Pennant gives institutional investors, and the advisors and companies they engage with, voting and governance intelligence to act on their own principles at scale. Legacy tools follow rigid rules; Pennant reasons through each ballot item, inbound email, and engagement question the way your team would, handling the clear calls and flagging the nuanced ones, keeping people in the driver's seat.

As one of our customers put it last week, “\[incumbent xyz\] can handle our routine stuff for another year, but we’re thrilled to use Pennant for the custom heavy-lifting that we’ve been wanting to do for a long time, and use you for everything from there.”

Pennant also serves the other side of the vote: public companies, law firms, and bankers who need to read their shareholder base and predict risk before the annual meeting. Same data, bigger market. We have a rare pairing: direct industry experience as the customer, plus the engineering chops to ship fast and earn trust.

After BlackRock, Ryan (CEO) was the customer for 6+ years, voting proxies at 3,000+ company meetings and advising Fortune 100 companies on how to win critical votes at PJT Partners. He used Glass Lewis and ISS every day.

Tommy (CTO) took the technical path, shipping products at BlackRock before earning his Harvard MBA and founding Mindware, where he built workflow-ready infrastructure for AI agents. launches.title: Florin: A full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters
launches.tagline: Autonomously places hard-to-price risks in seconds
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Florin is a full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters. Software takes a submission from a raw intake form to a bindable quote in seconds. Instead of matching a business to a class code, it verifies what the business actually does using satellite imagery, permits, public records and social media, then prices it by simulating tens of thousands of ways its next few years could go.

<https://youtu.be/BaXtkdP6_nc>

**What we do and why**

Insurance prices risk with class codes. An underwriter receives an application PDF, matches the business to a row in a rate table, and quotes off that row. This breaks in two ways. Applications are incomplete or wrong, so the price is built on bad inputs. And when a business does not fit any row, either because it is genuinely new (robotics, AI, autonomy) or because the table says the whole class or state is unprofitable, the answer is a declination. That is why carriers are exiting entire states and why a three-year-old industry can barely buy coverage at any price.

Florin replaces the table with evidence. It ingests the submission directly, no intake team. It builds its own picture of the business from the outside: aerial imagery of the actual premises, permits and public records, even the insured's social media, where it has caught operations that were never disclosed on the application. From that verified picture it runs simulations of the business's possible futures and produces a quote you can bind in seconds. No human touches the file.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109455&key=user_uploads/3776296/18477520-2b5a-4473-a727-92daf673768d)

\- Amol Pant was on Tesla's supercomputer team, designed rovers for NASA, and was early at a Thiel backed robotics startup

\- Aydin Sorensen was early at Terrafirma, a construction robotics company that recently raised $115M

Shaurya and I have been best friends since middle school, and Aydin and I were roommates in college. We all lived together in Seattle for 2 years.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** SpaceFlow is an AI-native procurement services company for businesses that make, move and serve physical goods. We help procurement teams bring more spend under management, execute source-to-contract work and turn identified savings into realized savings without adding headcount or replacing existing systems.

<https://youtu.be/lS9pBj_LeV8>

### The problem

Procurement must absorb changing demand, supplier issues, and growing volume without increasing cost or risking continuity. Every existing option fails on the same axis:

* **Internal teams:** expertise and judgment, fixed capacity. It takes years to build and when someone leaves, the tacit knowledge that keeps operations running is lost.
* **SaaS:** automation and visibility without execution. The customer still staffs the operation, supervises it, handles exceptions, and owns the result.
* **Outsourcing:** capacity, expertise, and accountability, permanently labor-linked. More volume, suppliers, and locations require more service-delivery headcount.

The unmet need is operating capacity that **takes responsibility for completing the work** while becoming faster, more consistent, and more profitable as volume grows.

## The insight

* **Software can recommend actions; it cannot assume commercial authority.** The customer keeps execution, exceptions, and supplier outcomes. Whoever owns the exceptions owns the expertise, and expertise is the entire product in procurement.
* **Incumbents cannot follow.** Consulting and outsourcing firms store process knowledge in employees and grow revenue through staff hours. Automation directly cannibalizes that model.
* **The economics are breakable.** Traditional services sit below software economics: Accenture at Rule-of-22.6, Genpact at 24.1. An AI-native operator can reach **Rule-of-60**.

## What we built

**The proprietary platform SpaceFlow uses to operate procurement for customers.**

* A **process-mapping engine** converts interviews, SOPs, approval rules, and existing system configurations into executable workflows. A supply-chain consultancy estimates it cuts customer launch from **26 months to 4**, a 6.5x jump in deployment capacity.
* It **executes procurement end to end**, from demand and production planning through sourcing, contracting, purchase orders, exception resolution, and reconciliation, across the customer's own systems.
* Operating across companies in the same vertical turns cross-company experience into **proprietary process and supplier intelligence**, while pooled demand creates **group-purchasing power**: better execution, prices, resilience, and terms for every customer.
* The same platform **monitors service levels, resolves exceptions, and remains accountable** for completing the operation. Per-action autonomy limits, approval queues, and an immutable audit log make every task provable.

## Proof so far

* **Live:** $400M a year of supplier spend under management, zero systems migrated. Multiple six figure contracts signed.
* **Demand for delegation:** our first customer cancelled 3 planned procurement hires, the CSCO invested his own money, and two chains are signing to progressively outsource purchasing, one planning a procurement team 90% smaller by 2027.
* **Results:** 3x faster RFQ cycles, off-contract spend down 42% at one customer, $120K a year saved at another.

## Where this goes

SpaceFlow will replace legacy service providers across the physical economy. Traditional service firms grow by hiring; SpaceFlow grows output faster than headcount, targeting **$1B in revenue with headcount capped at 100**. 

## What's in it for you?

1. **You run a physical-goods company with $100M+ supplier spend:** send us 12 months of PO history and we'll map one lane and size the savings, free. [spaceflow.tech](http://spaceflow.tech) · [emre@spaceflow.tech](mailto:emre@spaceflow.tech)
2. **You know an operator like that:** intros are gold.

**Emre Isik (CEO)**  studied computer engineering at the University of Cambridge and dropped the master's to build SpaceFlow full time. Before that he researched embedded AI for motor control at UCLA's Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics, published a machine-learning paper on reasoning with small data, and trained with Turkey's international informatics olympiad reserve team at 15. 

**Ali Eren Aytekin (co-founder)** left engineering at Istanbul Technical University to build SpaceFlow.  He was Microsoft Imagine Cup EMEA runner-up for a genetic-signal classifier that hit 98.3% accuracy, and co-authored the published paper on low-data reasoning. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-eren-aytekin-6305a41aa/) . He talked his way into an invite-only AI showcase in Istanbul, came out with a procurement problem from the CEO of a UK medical manufacturer, and shipped the solution with the team in two weeks. That deal became the learning SpaceFlow grew from.

**Hakan Enes Aksu (co-founder)** left information engineering at Boğaziçi University to build SpaceFlow. He has been shipping commercial software since 16, when his Reddit ad-automation service earned $40K in revenue, and he later built a tender-matching engine that reads public tenders against a company's product catalog and sold it to a corporate customer for five figures. name: Volaren Inc.
long_description:
Every great investment starts as an idea about the world. Institutions have teams of analysts turning those ideas into positions. Volaren is that team, processing data through fundamentals and quantitative models that can be personalized with AI.

Turn your views into trades, portfolios, and strategies, or co-invest alongside top traders and hedge funds. Volaren stays with you from there, showing you what's actually driving each position and what it means for your next move.
